Live-verified on this machine's real Hyprland 0.56.0 session: internal/input/hyprland.go's socket2 'globalshortcut>>' event never fires (confirmed with socat capture + real wtype keypress + direct hyprctl dispatch — zero bytes, hyprctl globalshortcuts stayed 'none'). Root cause: the 'global' dispatcher only activates a shortcut registered via the GlobalShortcuts D-Bus portal, which rejects a non-sandboxed Go binary with 'An app id is required' (confirmed live). Found the real working mechanism instead: native Wayland protocol hyprland_global_shortcuts_manager_v1, confirmed present in the registry, no portal/app-id gate. Also confirmed hyprctl keyword bindn is not idempotent (bind leak risk is real). Full details in a comment on this issue; epic Context & architecture corrected; fix tracked as copper-l2z.53.

Replaced the dead .socket2.sock globalshortcut>> watch with a hand-rolled client for hyprland_global_shortcuts_manager_v1 (the real Hyprland activation-delivery path, no portal/app-id gate); kept .socket.sock bindn/bindrn key registration unchanged and fixed its bind-leak (unconditional unbind before every bind). commit a8d33f0 on epic/copper-l2z.53.
